We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 3 reactions using templates 1914393, 1914394, 1914395 in this order.

We have applied 1914393 to target, got precursors: ('COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1'). So first reaction splits target into two fragments: fragment A (aryl amide with heterocycle) and fragment B (fluoro-cyclized amine with CCl aryl). Good.

Now need to apply template 1914394 to each fragment? The order is 1914393 then 1914394 then 1914395. Likely we apply 1914394 to one of the fragments (maybe the fragment B) to further break it. We attempted applying 1914394 to fragment A but got no result. Applying to fragment B gave precursors: ('ClCCl', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1'). So second reaction splits fragment B into ClCCl (dichloromethane?) and a simpler amine with phenyl.

Now need third reaction using template 1914395 on remaining fragments: we have three fragments now: fragment A (COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1), fragment C (FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1), and maybe ClCCl is a reagent? Actually ClCCl is dichloromethane, maybe a leaving group. But we need to apply 1914395 to something to get further precursors.

We need to retrieve template 1914395 to see what transformation it does.
